mainTopic: Strand counts of the priestly garments, prohibitions on damaging the בגדי כהונה and the ארון, and teachings about the משכן's boards
overview: This amud first finishes working out how many strands go into each thread of the בגדי כהונה. A גזירה שוה from the פרוכת teaches that the מעיל uses six strands. The גמרא debates whether the robe's own רמונים, which have eight strands, would be a better source. The tie is broken by the ברייתא's extra mention of שש. The פרוכת has 24 strands: four materials of six strands each. The חושן and אפוד have 28 strands, because one strand of זהב is added to each of the four materials, as רב אחא בר יעקב and רב אשי prove. Next, רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר rule that tearing בגדי כהונה, detaching the חושן from the אפוד, or removing the staves of the ארון brings מלקות. That holds because the פסוק says לא and not שלא. The staves could shift inside their rings but never came out. The amud then gives three readings of עצי שטים עומדים, and it ends with רבי חמא בר חנינא asking about בגדי השרד, a question answered on the next amud.

steps.title: The robe's threads learned from the curtain
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the מעיל says כליל תכלת. A גזירה שוה from the word תכלת in the פרוכת teaches that its threads are six-stranded.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Entirely of sky-blue." And we derive the word "sky-blue" here from the word "sky-blue" said about the curtain: just as there it is six, so too here it is six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a source derivation. It shows how we know the threads of the מעיל are made of six strands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the מעיל mentions only תכלת and does not say שש (six). So the number of strands is learned through a גזירה שוה. The word תכלת appears both here and by the פרוכת, and the פרוכת's threads are six-stranded, so the מעיל's threads are six-stranded too.

keyTerms.meaning: "Entirely of sky-blue" — the description of the robe in the פסוק
And he derives / and we learn
The curtain in the משכן / מקדש
Just as there, so too here — the standard גזירה שוה formula

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The words כליל תכלת are the end of a פסוק quoted from the previous section (שמות כח:לא, about the מעיל).

phrases.english: "entirely of sky-blue"
phrases.notes: End of the פסוק describing the robe (Exodus 28:31)

phrases.english: and derive "sky-blue"–"sky-blue" from the curtain:
phrases.notes: A verbal analogy (גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: just as there it is six,
so too here it is six.
phrases.notes: Per the Sefaria note, since the threads are also spun (doubled), each thread ends up with twelve strands

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation begun earlier about the strand count of the priestly garments
steps.raayaObject: The six-strand requirement for the threads of the מעיל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word תכלת, shared by the מעיל and the פרוכת

steps.title: Why not learn from the robe's own pomegranates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the strand count from the robe's hem pomegranates, which have eight strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us derive it instead from its hem and its pomegranates: just as there it is eight, so too here it should be eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the derivation from the פרוכת. It suggests a closer source: the pomegranates hanging on the robe's own hem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רמונים on the hem of the מעיל are made of eight-stranded threads. Since they are attached to the robe itself, it seems more natural to learn the robe's strand count from them. That would give eight strands, not six.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hem (the bottom edge of the robe)
Its pomegranates (woven decorations hanging from the hem)

phrases.english: Let us derive it from its hem and its pomegranates —
just as there it is eight,
so too here it should be eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of the פרוכת as the source for the comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from the פרוכת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A closer source exists, the robe's own pomegranates, and it would give a different number: eight instead of six.

steps.title: Compare a utensil to a utensil, not to an ornament
steps.stepSummary: It is better to learn a full item (the מעיל) from another full item (the פרוכת) than from a mere decoration (the רמונים).
steps.simpleTranslation: We derive a utensil from a utensil, and we do not derive a utensil from the ornament of a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the original derivation. It explains why the פרוכת is a better match than the pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעיל and the פרוכת are both complete, independent items. The רמונים are only decorations attached to the robe. A comparison works best between things of the same kind, so the פרוכת wins.

phrases.english: We derive a utensil from a utensil,
and we do not derive a utensil from the ornament of a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of preference for which source is more similar
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robe's own pomegranates are the closest source, so the robe should have eight strands.
steps.terutzMaskana: A complete item is compared to another complete item, so the פרוכת is the right source and the answer is six.

steps.title: On the contrary: compare an object to its own parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: learning the robe from its own pomegranates should be better than learning it from an unrelated item.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! We derive something from itself, and we do not derive something from elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the logic of the answer. It argues that the pomegranates are actually the better source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pomegranates are part of the מעיל itself. The פרוכת is a completely separate object. By this logic, closeness to the item itself outweighs being the same type of item, so the robe should have eight strands.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary — reverses the previous argument
Something from its own body / itself
From elsewhere / from an outside source

phrases.english: On the contrary: we derive something from itself,
and we do not derive something from elsewhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of preference given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a utensil is learned from a utensil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A competing rule of preference exists: learn an item from its own parts rather than from an outside item. That rule points back to eight strands.

steps.title: That is why the extra שש was needed
steps.stepSummary: Since both comparisons have strong logic, the ברייתא's extra mention of שש is what decides it. It teaches that garments without the word שש still need six strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we said: one mention is for the other garments, about which "six" was not stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument by pointing back to the ברייתא. One of the extra mentions of שש exists exactly to cover garments like the מעיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two comparisons cancel each other out, so logic alone cannot decide. That is precisely why the ברייתא used one of the five mentions of שש to include "other garments where שש is not written." This extra source fixes the מעיל at six strands, not eight.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we said — points back to an earlier source that already solves the issue
Fine linen; read here as hinting at "six" strands

steps.whatToRemember: The מעיל's threads are six-stranded. Two competing comparisons (the פרוכת versus the robe's own רמונים) seem evenly matched. The tie is broken by the ברייתא's extra שש, which includes garments that do not mention שש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic pattern: when two lines of reasoning conflict, an extra word in the פסוק (a ריבוי) is what decides the הלכה.

phrases.english: This is what we said:
"for the other garments about which 'six' was not stated."
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא's use of one of the five mentions of שש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock created by step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an extra textual source in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning from the robe's own pomegranates is equally strong, so the robe might have eight strands.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra שש explicitly includes garments without the word שש, which confirms six strands for the מעיל.

steps.title: The curtain's 24 strands are obvious
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the פרוכת's threads have 24 strands. This is simply four materials times six strands each, and needs no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The curtain: twenty-four. Four materials of six strands each — there is neither judgment nor judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the ברייתא, about the פרוכת. It explains where the number 24 comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוכת is woven from four materials: שש, תכלת, ארגמן, and תולעת שני. Each one is six-stranded, so four times six equals 24. The phrase לא דינא ולא דיינא means this is so clear that no argument is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither judgment nor judge — it is completely obvious and needs no proof

phrases.english: The curtain: twenty-four —
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא

phrases.english: four materials of six strands each,
there is neither judgment nor judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next clause of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each thread of the פרוכת has 24 strands: four materials of six strands each. This is self-evident.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the breastplate and ephod have 28 strands?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said the threads of the חושן and אפוד have 28 strands. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The breastplate and the ephod have twenty-eight strands. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the פרוכת's 24, which was simple math with no need for proof, the number 28 is not obvious. So the גמרא asks for a source in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The breastplate worn by the כהן גדול
The apron-like garment of the כהן גדול
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The breastplate and ephod: twenty-eight
phrases.notes: Quoting the next clause of the ברייתא

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פרוכת's 24 strands to the next item in the ברייתא, the חושן and אפוד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the 28-strand count of the חושן and אפוד.

steps.title: Four colors of six strands plus four strands of gold
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists זהב along with four other materials. Four materials at six strands each make 24, and four strands of זהב bring the total to 28.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall make a breastplate of judgment, the work of a skilled craftsman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: gold, sky-blue, purple, scarlet, and twisted linen.' Four materials of six strands each make twenty-four. Gold adds four. That makes twenty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that lists the materials of the חושן. It adds up the strands to reach 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four materials תכלת, ארגמן, תולעת שני and שש each have six strands, which gives 24, just like the פרוכת. The new ingredient here is זהב, which adds only four strands. The total is 28.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of a skilled craftsman (a special weave)

steps.confusionAlert: The four gold strands are four in total, not four per color. Only the other four materials have six strands each.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall make a breastplate of judgment
the work of a skilled craftsman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it
gold, sky-blue, and purple
and scarlet, and twisted fine linen'
phrases.notes: שמות כ״ח:ט״ו

phrases.english: four materials of six each make twenty-four
gold adds four
so there are twenty-eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק lists the four six-strand materials plus זהב. 24 plus 4 gold strands equals 28.

steps.title: Why not make the gold six strands too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that זהב has only four strands. Why not six, like every other material?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the gold is also six strands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the number four for the gold. Every other material has six strands, so why should gold be different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 taught that six is the default even when the word שש is not written. By that logic זהב should also be six, which would make the total 30, not 28. The next two steps defend the number four.

phrases.english: But say that the gold is also six!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'gold is four' part of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the זהב has only four strands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the other materials follow a six-strand default, so the gold should follow it too.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: the word 'cords' teaches four
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from the plural word פתילים that the gold has four strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says 'and cut it into cords.' One 'cord' means two strands, and 'cords' means two of those. That makes four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that a פסוק about the gold itself points to four strands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פתיל is a folded strand, which counts as two. The plural פתילים means at least two such cords, so 2 + 2 = 4. Because the Torah gives the gold its own count, the six-strand default does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cord (a doubled strand, counting as two)
Cords (plural, meaning at least two cords)

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said,
the verse says: 'And he cut it into cords.'
phrases.notes: שמות ל״ט:ג׳

phrases.english: 'Cord' is two; 'cords' is two of those
so here there are four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source that sets a specific count for the gold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gold should follow the six-strand default.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural פתילים fixes the gold at four strands.

steps.title: רב אשי: the gold must be split evenly into each color
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves four from the fact that the gold is worked into each of the four materials. The only even split that fits is one strand per material.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The verse says 'to work it into the sky-blue and into the purple.' How should we do it? If we make four gold threads of two strands each, that is eight. If we make two threads of two strands and two threads of one strand, that does not work, because 'and you shall make' teaches that all its makings must be equal. So it must be one strand in each, which is four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer. Because the gold is mixed into each of the four materials, the numbers only work out if the gold has four strands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold must be divided among four materials. Six cannot be split evenly into four (2, 2, 1, 1), and ועשית demands that every part be equal. Two strands each would make eight, which is even more than six, so the only option is one strand per material, four in total.

keyTerms.meaning: All its makings must be equal

steps.whatToRemember: The חושן and אפוד threads have 28 strands: 6 strands each of תכלת, ארגמן, תולעת שני and שש, plus 1 strand of זהב twisted into each of those four.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: the verse says:
'To work it into the sky-blue
and into the purple.'
phrases.notes: The verse continues with the scarlet and linen, so there are four materials

phrases.english: How should we do it?
If we make four gold threads of two strands each
that makes eight.
phrases.notes: Even more than six, so this does not fit

phrases.english: If we make two threads of two strands each
and two threads of one strand each (making six)
the verse says 'and you shall make'
which teaches that all its makings must be equal.
phrases.notes: So it must be one strand per material, four in total

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Process of elimination using an even-division requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Six gold strands could be spread among the four materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: Equal division requires one strand per material, four in total.

steps.title: Tearing priestly garments earns lashes
steps.stepSummary: רחבא quotes רב יהודה that one who tears בגדי כהונה receives מלקות, learned from the words לא יקרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבא said in the name of רב יהודה: One who tears priestly garments receives lashes, as it says: 'It shall not be torn.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יהודה rules that deliberately tearing בגדי כהונה is a לאו punished with מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the opening of the מעיל says לא יקרע. רב יהודה reads this as a prohibition, and he applies it to all בגדי כהונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the prohibition against damaging בגדי כהונה.

phrases.english: Rachava said that Rav Yehuda said:
One who tears priestly garments is lashed,
as it is stated: 'It shall not be torn.'
phrases.notes: שמות כ״ח:ל״ב, about the opening of the מעיל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the בגדי כהונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberately tearing בגדי כהונה is a לאו punished with מלקות.

steps.title: Maybe 'it shall not be torn' is just a reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב suggests the פסוק is only explaining why the opening gets a hem, so that it won't tear, and is not stating a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: Maybe this is what the Merciful One is saying: make a hem for it so that it will not tear!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges רב יהודה's reading. He suggests the words are a reason, not a command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לא יקרע only explains the purpose of the hem, then there is no לאו here. Without a לאו, there would be no מלקות for tearing.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected to this:
But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
Make a hem for it
so that it will not tear!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading of לא יקרע as a לאו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could be a purpose clause explaining the hem, not a prohibition.

steps.title: The verse does not say 'so that it not tear'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the objection. The פסוק says לא, not שלא, so it is a command.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'so that it not be torn'? No, so it is a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אחא בר יעקב's reading by looking at the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reason would be written שלא יקרע, meaning 'so that it not tear.' The פסוק says לא יקרע, which is the language of a command. So רב יהודה's ruling of מלקות stands.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it not be torn (purpose wording)

steps.whatToRemember: Because the פסוק says לא יקרע and not שלא יקרע, tearing בגדי כהונה is a real לאו punished with מלקות.

phrases.english: Is it written 'so that it not be torn'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 13 and upholds step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The full objection of רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's wording is a command (לא), not a purpose clause (שלא).

steps.title: Separating the breastplate or removing the Ark's staves earns lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that someone who detaches the חושן from the אפוד, or pulls the staves out of the ארון, receives מלקות, based on the words לא יזח and לא יסורו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Someone who detaches the breastplate from the ephod, or who removes the staves of the Ark, gets lashes. The Torah says 'it shall not be detached' and 'they shall not be removed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new ruling. It follows the same pattern as רב יהודה's rule about tearing בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as לא יקרע made tearing the כהן's clothing a punishable sin, the words לא יזח and לא יסורו make these two actions punishable. Each phrase is read as a real לאו (negative command), and breaking a לאו brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: One who detaches or loosens (from the root זח, to move away)
The apron-like garment of the כהן גדול; the חושן is tied to it
The carrying poles (staves) of the Ark

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds two more permanent לאוין connected to the משכן and the בגדי כהונה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
One who detaches the breastplate from upon the ephod,
and one who removes the staves of the Ark, is lashed,
phrases.notes: Meaning he takes them out of their rings.

phrases.english: as it says: 'It shall not be detached' and 'they shall not be removed.'
phrases.notes: שמות כח:כח and שמות כה:טו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of derivation as רב יהודה's לא יקרע teaching to two new cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Detaching the חושן from the אפוד or removing the בדי ארון is a לאו punished with מלקות.

steps.title: Maybe the verse only explains why they were fastened tightly
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב suggests these פסוקים are not commands. They may only tell us to fasten the items well so that they will not come apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: Maybe when the Torah said this, it meant: tie them tightly and make them well, so that it won't come loose and they won't come out!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges רבי אלעזר using the same argument he used against רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim is that לא יזח and לא יסורו describe the purpose of the construction: build it firmly so it stays together. If so, these words are not prohibitions, and there would be no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, i.e., the Torah

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected to this:
But perhaps when the Merciful One said this,
it means: fasten them and make them well
so that it won't come loose and they won't be removed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source of רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading of לא יזח and לא יסורו as prohibitions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could be a reason for building it firmly, not a command. Without a command, there is no מלקות.

steps.title: The verse says 'not', not 'so that it not'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the objection. The פסוק does not say שלא, which would be a reason. It says לא, which is a command.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'so that it won't be detached' or 'so that they won't be removed'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא בר יעקב exactly as it did in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah only meant to give a reason, it would have written שלא ("so that it not"). Since it wrote plain לא, the words are a direct command, so רבי אלעזר's מלקות stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a rhetorical question showing the text says otherwise)
So that it not; this wording would express purpose

steps.whatToRemember: לא יזח and לא יסורו are real prohibitions. Separating the חושן from the אפוד, or removing the staves of the ארון, earns מלקות.

phrases.english: Is it written 'so that it won't be detached' and 'so that they won't be removed'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the objection of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects רב אחא בר יעקב's reading
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His reading needs the word שלא, but the פסוק says לא.

steps.title: Two verses about the staves seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא points out a contradiction. One פסוק says the staves never leave the rings. Another says the staves are put into the rings, which suggests they were out at some point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא raised a contradiction. It is written: 'The staves shall be in the rings of the Ark; they shall not be removed from it.' But it is also written: 'And its staves shall be brought into the rings'!
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא points to two פסוקים about the ארון's staves that seem to clash. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק means the staves are always inside the rings. The second פסוק speaks of placing them in the rings, as if they come in and out. Both cannot seem true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction between two sources
Rings attached to the ארון that hold the staves
And it shall be brought in

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי אלעזר. It is a separate question about how two פסוקים fit together.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא רָמֵי, כְּתִיב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina raised a contradiction. It is written:
'In the rings of the Ark the staves shall be;
they shall not be removed from it,'
phrases.notes: שמות כה:טו

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And its staves shall be brought into the rings'!
phrases.notes: שמות כז:ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the פסוק לא יסורו from רבי אלעזר's ruling and raises a new textual problem with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of לא יסורו ממנו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says the staves never leave the rings. Another describes putting them in, which suggests they do leave.

steps.title: The staves could shift but never came out
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the staves could move back and forth inside the rings, but they never slipped all the way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? They could be moved about, but they did not come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא resolves his own contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: והובא refers to sliding the staves forward or back within the rings. לא יסורו means they were never fully removed. Sefaria explains that the staves were thick at the ends and thin in the middle, so once forced into the rings they could slide but not slip out.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this so? (a formula that introduces a reconciliation)
They could be loosened or moved about

phrases.english: How is this so?
They can be shifted, but they do not slip out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק describes a different part of the reality (harmonization)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים seemed to disagree about whether the staves ever leave the rings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The staves move inside the rings (והובא) but are never fully removed (לא יסורו).

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same resolution
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same point. Each פסוק stops us from over-reading the other, and the conclusion is מתפרקין ואין נשמטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches this too. 'The staves shall be in the rings of the Ark.' I might think they may not move from their place at all. So the Torah says: 'And its staves shall be brought into the rings.' If it only said 'its staves shall be brought,' I might think they go in and out. So the Torah says: 'The staves shall be in the rings of the Ark.' How so? They shift, but they do not come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows each פסוק balancing the other. The first alone would mean the staves never move at all. The second alone would mean they come fully in and out. Together they produce the middle position: they move, but they stay in.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
Therefore the פסוק says (to rule out that thought)

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
'In the rings of the Ark the staves shall be.'
One might think they may not move from their place at all?
Therefore the verse says: 'And its staves shall be brought into the rings.'
If it only said 'and its staves shall be brought,'
one might think they go in and come out entirely.
Therefore the verse says: 'In the rings of the Ark the staves shall be.'
How so? They shift, but they do not slip out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the two פסוקים against each other
steps.whatToRemember: The ארון's staves could slide inside the rings but were never removed. This is how both פסוקים are true.

steps.title: The boards stood the way they grew
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains עצי שטים עומדים: the boards of the משכן were set up in the same direction the tree grew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: What does 'acacia wood, standing' mean? That they stand the way they grew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about the boards of the משכן. This is the first of three explanations of the word עומדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עומדים looks extra. רבי חמא reads it as an instruction: each board was set upright with its bottom down, the way it grew as a tree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
Acacia wood, used for the boards of the משכן

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is meant by what is written: 'acacia wood, standing'?
phrases.notes: שמות כו:טו

phrases.english: That they stand in the direction they grew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic connected to the earlier one only because both concern the משכן's wooden parts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boards of the משכן were set upright in their natural growing direction.

steps.title: The boards held their gold plating in place
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: עומדים means the boards held up their gold plating so it would not fall off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'standing' means they hold their plating in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reading of the same word עומדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word describes what the wood did, not how it was positioned. The wood held the gold covering firmly in place.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'standing'
means that they hold their plating in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of עומדים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boards held up their gold plating.

steps.title: The boards last forever
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: עומדים teaches that the boards of the משכן were not lost forever. They stand for all time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'standing.' You might say their hope is gone and their chance is over. So the Torah says 'standing': they stand forever and ever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reading of עומדים, this time a message of hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once the משכן was put away, its boards were finished and gone. The word עומדים teaches that they endure forever and are not lost.
steps.whatToRemember: עומדים has three readings: the boards stood as they grew, they held their gold plating, and they last forever.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'standing.'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר אָבַד סִבְרָן וּבָטֵל סִכּוּיָין —
phrases.english: Lest you say their hope is lost and their prospect is cancelled,
the verse says: 'standing,'
meaning that they stand forever and ever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation of עומדים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משכן's boards endure forever and are not lost.

steps.title: What does "בגדי השרד" mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא quotes the פסוק "את בגדי השרד לשרת בקודש" and asks what it is teaching. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: What is the meaning of what is written, "the שרד garments, for serving in the holy place"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to talking about the בגדי כהונה. רבי חמא בר חנינא quotes a פסוק and asks what it means, setting up his explanation on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שרד is unusual, so the question is why the תורה uses it to describe the priestly clothing. This line only asks the question. The explanation that follows will build a lesson out of this word.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (a formula that opens an explanation of a פסוק)
The שרד garments, the special clothing worn for the עבודה
To serve, meaning to do the עבודה
In the holy place, the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to anything earlier. It is the opening question of a new explanation, and the answer comes right on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said:
phrases.notes: Attribution, merged into this step.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of that which is written:
phrases.notes: Opens an explanation of a פסוק.

phrases.english: "The serad garments
phrases.notes: The unusual word שרד is what needs explaining.

phrases.english: for serving in the Sanctuary"
phrases.notes: שמות לה:יט. The dash shows the answer is coming next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי חמא בר חנינא מאי דכתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanations of עצי שטים עומדים, the גמרא now turns to a different פסוק about the בגדי כהונה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק call the priestly garments "בגדי השרד", and what lesson does that wording teach?
